text: Most people use AI app builders to make random projects they never launch. A fake SaaS. A dashboard nobody asked for. A landing page that never gets published. But if you want to actually make money with AI, the better move is simple. Find a real business with a real problem, build them something useful, and charge for the result. In this video, I'm going to show you how I would use Hanzo dot A I to make my first one thousand dollars building apps and websites for clients.
We'll go from finding the client, to packaging the offer, to building the first draft inside Hanzo, to delivering the final project and getting paid.

The first step is not selling AI. Most business owners do not wake up thinking, I need an AI transformation platform. They think: I need more leads. I need more bookings. My website looks old. My form does not work. My business does not look professional online. I started building something with AI and got stuck. So instead of selling AI, sell the outcome. A better booking page. A website that works on mobile. A lead capture page. A client portal. A simple app for their customers. Or a finished version of the website they already started. That is what makes the offer easy to understand.

Now you need to find businesses with obvious problems. Search for local businesses like med spas, contractors, salons, coaches, restaurants, real estate agents, photographers, consultants, cleaners, landscapers, and fitness trainers. Look for businesses with no website, an outdated website, bad mobile design, no booking button, no lead form, or a confusing customer flow.

The easiest outreach message is specific. You can say: Hey, I came across your business and noticed your booking flow is hard to use on mobile. I build simple mobile-friendly websites and booking pages for local businesses. I can put together a cleaner version this week if you want to take a look. That works because you are pointing to one problem and offering one fix.

Now package the offer. For your first few projects, keep it simple. A landing page can be five hundred dollars. A business website can be seven hundred fifty dollars. A simple app, booking system, lead capture page, or client portal can be one thousand dollars. The one thousand dollar offer should include the build, mobile-friendly design, contact form or booking call to action, client content added, one revision round, and launch support. Do not include unlimited changes. Do not include months of maintenance. Do not include complex integrations unless they pay extra.

Before you build anything, run a discovery call. Ask: What do you want this app or website to do? Do you want more leads, bookings, calls, sales, or signups? Who is your ideal customer? What services need to be included? Do you already have a logo, photos, colors, or copy? Do you need a booking link, contact form, payment button, quote form, gallery, or client portal? Then repeat the scope back to them. So what I'm hearing is: you need a clean mobile-friendly website with your services, testimonials, booking button, and contact form. The goal is to look more professional and get more inquiries. I can build that for one thousand dollars. That is how you turn the conversation into a project.

Do not start without a deposit. For a one thousand dollar project, charge fifty percent upfront and fifty percent before final handoff. That means five hundred dollars to start and five hundred dollars before delivery.

Now we build in Hanzo. Start with a clear prompt. Do not just say, build a website. Give Hanzo the business type, the goal, the sections, the style, and the action you want customers to take. For example: Build a modern one-page website for a local med spa. The goal is to get more appointment bookings. Include a hero section, services, before-and-after gallery, testimonials, F A Q, and a strong booking call to action. Make the design premium, clean, trustworthy, and mobile-friendly. Once Hanzo creates the first version, your job is to direct it. Ask it to improve the headline. Ask it to make the call-to-action stronger. Ask it to rewrite the services section. Ask it to make the mobile version easier to scan. Ask it to remove anything generic. The client is not paying you because you typed one prompt. They are paying you because you know what to ask for, what to fix, and how to turn the first draft into something usable.

When the first version is ready, send it as a draft. Do not say, here is the final site. Say: I put together the first draft. The structure is in place, and now I'd love your feedback on the services, photos, contact info, and booking call-to-action before I do the final polish. Then ask specific questions. Is the information accurate? Are the services correct? Do you want any photos replaced? Is the booking link right? Is the phone number and email correct?

Before final delivery, test everything. Click every button. Submit every form. Check mobile. Check spelling. Check the booking link. Check the phone number. Check the email. Then send the final invoice before full handoff. You can say: The final version is ready. Once the remaining balance is paid, I'll send over the live link, access details, and a quick walkthrough. That is professional, and it prevents you from chasing payment after the client already has everything.

The easiest way to make more than one thousand dollars is offering monthly support after launch. You can help with updates, S E O setup, Google Business Profile cleanup, new landing pages, analytics, chatbot setup, lead follow-up, or maintenance. A simple upsell sounds like: Now that the site is live, I can also help maintain it monthly, add new offers, improve S E O, and make sure everything keeps working. That can be one hundred, two hundred fifty, or five hundred dollars per month depending on what you include. So one one-thousand-dollar build can become recurring revenue.

The system is simple. Find a business with a visible problem. Offer a clear result. Collect a deposit. Build the first draft in Hanzo. Send it for specific feedback. Revise once. Test everything. Collect final payment. Offer monthly support. You do not need to be a giant agency. You need to solve one real problem for one real business. That is how you make your first one thousand dollars with Hanzo dot A I app builder.
